questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel too far in the opposite direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward oncoming traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to skid, stay calm. Steer in the direction the car is sliding.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?

options.text: Drive faster to get to your destination quicker.
Stay closer to the car ahead of you.
Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: When driving on wet roads, increase the space between you and the car in front of you.

questions.question: Turn signals must be visible from how far away?

options.text: 500 feet.
250 feet.
300 feet.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet.
questions.explanation: Turn signals must be visible from 300 feet away during daylight hours.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect how far a vehicle travels before stopping?

options.text: How fast you react.
What time of day it is.
How good your brakes are.
What condition your tires are in.

questions.correctAnswerText: What time of day it is.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, road conditions, your vehicle's weight, brake condition, tire condition, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
People crossing the road ahead.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: People crossing the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers of hazards ahead. This sign means people may be crossing the road.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but many cars are coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection instead.
Wait at the edge of the road for traffic to clear.
Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left and oncoming traffic is coming, you can move into the intersection when the light is green. Wait in the middle for oncoming traffic to pass before you turn.

questions.question: When you turn left onto a one-way street, which lane should you use?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Any lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At unmarked railroad crossings, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait for the train to pass.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving the same direction. A broken line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, what is the best way to merge?

options.text: Drive slowly and wait for an opening.
Drive faster than freeway traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic so you blend in smoothly and safely. Vehicles entering must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a low ground railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. The bottom of low vehicles may drag or get caught on the tracks.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic moving in opposite directions, you should:

options.text: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, move back to the right side as soon as there is enough space between you and the other vehicle.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time:

options.text: The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.
The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way.
The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go if the way is clear.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you see this sign, you are going the wrong way on a one-way street. You risk a head-on collision. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only the driver on the broken line side can pass.

questions.question: You may cross a solid yellow line:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During the day only.
At any time.
When turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. You may only cross a solid yellow line when making a turn.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
Slow down and let it pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights and/or siren, move to the right side of the road as far as safely possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to stop for a red or yellow light.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm is raised upward, it means they are turning right. Change your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower cars on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down before entering the exit ramp. Slow down only after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs show?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Be extra careful and watch for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: You see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line on the road. The broken line is next to your lane. When can you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Only on an expressway.
When there is no oncoming traffic.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is no oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you can pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.

questions.question: You are driving past a car that just parked on the side of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Expect the driver to open the door as you pass.
Speed up.
Hit your brakes hard.
Expect the driver to wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, assume the driver may open the door as you approach. Drive with extra caution near parked vehicles.

questions.question: You need to back out of your driveway. Children are playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check if the way is clear.
Tell the children to move away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and check behind your car before backing up, especially when children are nearby. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Any lights work the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What color are signs that show public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show public recreation areas and places of historical importance. They help you find attractions when traveling.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt.
The steering wheel.
Your rearview mirror.
Your seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat.
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights.
Flashing yellow lights.
White lines on the side of the road.
White arrows on the road in the middle of lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows on the road in the middle of lanes.
questions.explanation: Arrows on the road show which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: An area where passing is not allowed.
A one-way traffic area.
The blind spot around a large truck.
An area for motor vehicles only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot around a large truck.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around large trucks where drivers cannot see you. Stay away from these areas.
